content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to find precursors and templates.

We can break down target into two main fragments: a sulfonamide linking two aryl rings, and an amide attached to a phenyl with an aniline (NH2) at para? Actually structure: a tolyl (methyl phenyl) attached via sulfonamide to another phenyl which is para-substituted with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (C=C-C(=O)N-phenyl-NH2). So overall: tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2 (an aniline). So retrosynthesis could be:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide: target -> tolyl amine (p-methyl aniline) + sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl aryl) + second aryl amine? Actually sulfonamide formed between tolyl amine (p-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) phenyl sulfonyl chloride. So we can break at S-N bond: produce tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl aryl). The sulfonyl chloride could be made from the second aryl sulfonyl chloride (4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) phenyl sulfonyl chloride). That could be made from the corresponding phenyl sulfonic acid then chlorination.

Alternatively, we could form the sulfonamide via coupling of sulfonyl chloride with aniline.

Step 2: The second aryl sulfonyl chloride could be derived from the aryl sulfonic acid, which could be made from sulfonation of the phenyl ring (electrophilic aromatic substitution) using SO3 or chlorosulfonic acid on the phenyl bearing the side chain (the side chain could be introduced later). But maybe easier: start from 4-bromo phenyl sulfonyl chloride then do Suzuki coupling to attach the side chain? However we need <=3 steps total.

Maybe better: Disconnection at the amide bond: produce the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) and aniline (aniline). The amide could be formed via coupling of aniline (aniline) with the acid chloride of the cinnamic acid derivative. The cinnamic acid derivative is 4-(CH=CH-COOH) phenyl (para). That could be made via Heck coupling of 4-bromobenzaldehyde with acrylate then oxidation? Or via Knoevenagel condensation of 4-formyl phenyl with malonic acid then decarboxylation? Might be many steps.

Given limit 3 steps, we need a concise route: maybe use commercially available building blocks: p-toluidine (commercial), 4-aminophenyl (aniline) (commercial), 4-(2-oxo-2-phenylamino)phenyl? Not.

Let's search for commercially available sulfonyl chloride with appropriate substitution: maybe "4-(2-oxo-2-phenylamino)phenylsulfonyl chloride". Likely not.

Alternative: Use sulfonylation of aniline with sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) phenyl sulfonyl chloride. Could we get that sulfonyl chloride from commercially available "4-(2-oxo-2-phenylamino)phenylsulfonyl chloride"? Not sure.

Maybe we can propose a route with three steps:

1. Form the amide: React aniline (c3ccccc3N) with trans-cinnamoyl chloride (ClC(=O)C=Cc1ccc(cc1)Cl?) Actually trans-cinnamoyl chloride is commercially available (C=CC(=O)Cl). But we need the phenyl attached to the amide nitrogen (anilide). So we need N-phenylcinnamamide (cinnamoyl anilide). That's product of aniline + trans-cinnamoyl chloride. That gives C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1 (no extra phenyl). But our target has additional phenyl attached to the double bond (the phenyl is the same as the aniline? Wait structure: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. The double bond is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the side chain is attached to phenyl ring at para position: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline. So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide is N-phenylcinnamamide (cinnamoyl attached to aniline). That's exactly formed by reacting aniline with trans-cinnamoyl chloride. So product is C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1 (no extra phenyl on the double bond). Wait cinnamoyl chloride is ClC(=O)C=CH-Ph? Actually cinnamoyl chloride is ClC(=O)C=CH-Ph (phenyl attached to the double bond). So yes, trans-cinnamoyl chloride has phenyl attached to the double bond. So reacting aniline with cinnamoyl chloride yields trans-cinnamoyl anilide: /C=C/C(=O)Nc1ccccc1. That's exactly the side chain part (without the extra phenyl ring? The side chain includes the phenyl attached to the double bond (c2ccc...). So the product is the side chain attached to phenyl ring (the phenyl that is sulfonylated). So we need the phenyl bearing the sulfonyl group also bearing the cinnamoyl anilide at para position. So we need to attach the cinnamoyl anilide to a phenyl ring that also will be sulfonylated.

Thus we could start from 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) which we can sulfonylate? Actually we need a phenyl with both sulfonyl group (attached to S) and the side chain (cinnamoyl anilide). The sulfonyl group attaches via nitrogen (sulfonamide) to tolyl amine. So the phenyl ring is the sulfonyl aryl (Ar-SO2-). So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride with para side chain (cinnamoyl anilide). That could be synthesized by first forming the side chain on a phenyl (e.g., 4-bromobenzaldehyde -> Wittig -> etc) then convert to sulfonyl chloride.

But limited steps.

Maybe we can propose a convergent route: Step 1: Synthesize the sulfonyl chloride from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) via Suzuki coupling with phenyl vinyl (cinnamoyl anilide) boronic acid? Not.

Alternative: Use sulfonylation after amide formation: first make the anilide side chain attached to phenyl (i.e., 4-(cinnamoyl anilide)aniline?), then sulfonylate the aniline with tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonamide formation is between sulfonyl chloride and aniline. So we could have the phenyl bearing the side chain as an aniline (NH2) which we then sulfonylate with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl). That would give the target: p-toluenesulfonyl attached to the phenyl via N (forming sulfonamide). The phenyl also has the side chain attached at para? Wait the phenyl bearing side chain is the same phenyl that is sulfonylated? In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via N (sulfonamide) and the phenyl also has the side chain at para relative to the sulfonamide? Let's examine SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

First phenyl: c1ccc(... )cc1 with methyl (C) at position 1 (para? Actually methyl attached to aromatic carbon before ring). So tolyl ring with sulfonamide attached at para? The NS(=O)(=O) attached to the tolyl ring at position 4 (para to methyl). Then the sulfonyl group attaches to second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). That second phenyl has the side chain /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N at para position relative to sulfonyl group. So the second phenyl is a phenyl sulfonyl (Ar-SO2-) attached to tolyl via N. The second phenyl also has the side chain at para.

Thus we can think of building the second phenyl as an aniline (para-aminophenyl) that we first acylate (amide) then sulfonylate? Actually the sulfonyl group attaches to the nitrogen of the sulfonamide, not to the phenyl directly. The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl as part of the sulfonyl group (Ar-SO2-). So the second phenyl is part of the sulfonyl group, not an aniline. So we need to create sulfonyl chloride of that phenyl (Ar-SO2Cl) then react with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide.

Thus route:

Step A: Prepare 4-(cinnamoyl anilide)benzenesulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl with para side chain). Then react with p-toluidine to give target.

Now we need to make that sulfonyl chloride in <=2 steps (since total 3 steps). Could be made from 4-(cinnamoyl anilide)benzenesulfonic acid (commercial?) maybe not. Could be made from 4-(cinnamoyl anilide)benzenesulfonyl chloride directly (maybe commercially available). Let's check if such compound is available. Use search catalog?
